The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
5,\,15,\,45,\,135,\,…
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =3 \\  & =\frac{15}{5} \\  & =\frac{45}{15} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1}=5({3}^{n-1})=\frac{5}{3}(3)^{n}.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A={\frac{5}{3}(3)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}(3)^{N} & =7\,971\,615 \\ {3}^{N} & =4\,782\,969 \\ N & ={log}_{3}⁡(4\,782\,969) \\ N & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(4\,782\,969)}{{log}_{10}⁡(3)} \\ N & =14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={\frac{5}{3}(3)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 14}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $14$ elements, we must have $|A|=14.$
